title: Four Consecutive Slashes
text: The costumes changed every year, but among them there was a vampire one! Ah, it was splendid, I say. A costume you might even see at an idol concert! Father, too, ought to suit a vampire costume perfectly.
Whenever I picture Father at Halloween, though… for some reason all that comes to mind is him in a Peckul mascot suit. And he looked thoroughly annoyed about it even then.

In the very first year, Big Sister eagerly prepared a Raph-species mascot costume, only to have Big Sister stop him. Then Father put bat wings on the Raph-species costume and wore a faint smile. Incidentally, Father also tried to do a mummy costume, but Big Sister stopped him for that too. I confess I’m not too keen on Father as a mummy either.

Because… somehow all I can picture is Father covered in blood. Older Sister kept trying to get Father into a cat costume. Panda got turned into a skull via body paint by Father. That one time, even Panda didn’t seem to mind and wore the costume without complaint.
“Actually, which is it, I wonder? Motoyasu-san in his original form, or Motoyasu-san as a Usaunny?”
“Could you not fixate on that, please?”
“Motoyasu’s got good looks, so a vampire getup would definitely suit him.”
“That goes for Ren and Itsuki too, doesn’t it…”
Shall we all do vampire cosplay, I wonder!
“So in the end, nano, did we figure out the origin of that unknown settlement’s name?”
“No, no… even if some legend said ‘this is the hint,’ there’s no way you’d actually arrive at the answer from that. It’s a mystery even a great detective would be stunned by.”

“That’s certainly true. Using island-derived equipment to cast transformation magic, coming to the dungeon, and then working a hidden castle mechanism via totem pole just to get in—that’s way too much.”
“Well, there was someone working in the shadows behind it all… if you say it’s just a leftover trace of that, it’s plausible enough.”
Amid Father and the others’ conversation, I heard the flap-flap sound of Rival’s wings beating.
“Now that I think about it, I feel like I once heard that ‘Dracula,’ the word for vampire, means ‘son of the dragon’ in some language or other.”
Father said this, muttering as though he were looking at Rival while he spoke.
“Are vampires dragons?”
“Nano?”

“This is about dragons that don’t actually exist in my world, but apparently in some places ‘dragon’ can also mean ‘demon.’ I think it’s a holdover from a time when those two ideas got mixed together.”
“In this world they’re just lovesick creatures who only look the part!”
“Say whatever you want, nanoon!”
Rival brushed off Ren’s remark like it was nothing.
“In other words, you’re saying vampire cosplay is dragon cosplay, so I should quit it! Father!”
If it’s a getup derived from dragons, then I, Motoyasu, cannot possibly do it. Now that I think it over carefully, vampires do grow bat wings and the like. Indeed, that is rather dragon-like.
“That’s not really what I meant, but… Yuki-chan, what do you think?”
“What exactly does a vampire look like? Is it a dragon’s appearance?”
“Honestly… it’s basically the outfit Count Hagenburg, who manages the hotel here on Cal Mira Island, wears when greeting guests.”
“Isn’t that just a plain tailcoat?”
“Add a black cape to that, and that’s about the feel of it.”
“Then it’s not a dragon at all! I think it would suit Motoyasu-sama wonderfully!”
Since Yuki-chan was sending me such encouragement, this called for a decisive pose! The pose of a raging Filolial-sama! Kweh!
“Why the sudden pose… you’re a Usaunny, so it doesn’t really land with any impact.”
“I feel like I just pressed the ‘strike a pointless pose’ button.”
“Yeah, pretty much.”
“Motoyasu-sama! Fight on!”
Spurred on by Yuki-chan’s cheering, I pressed steadily onward!
“But you know, I was just thinking. Vampires are a pretty common motif in edgy chuunibyou settings, but Ren, you don’t seem all that into it?”
“Don’t drag me into this.”
“Incidentally, the Ren from the first world, the one close with Fleon-chan, has done vampire cosplay before, I say!”
“Shut up, Motoyasu!”
Even as I fought on, Ren hurled jeers at me! What is this! I’m merely supplementing the discussion, I say!
“It’s that thing, you know. I do have the general concept of vampires—something about blood as a medium—but I might not have dug that deeply into actual vampire lore.”
“No, judging by Ren’s reaction, he probably knows a fair bit. He just didn’t happen to know about the game where you storm a castle to defeat a vampire.”
“Don’t try to analyze me. I graduated from that phase. Keep this up and you’ll summon Kuro and Fleon.”
“Who knows… Ren-san, you did put off the surgery to remove your Filolial wings for a while, so if you added bat—er, dragon wings to your back, you’d probably be delighted.”
“Oh, we’ve got a costume item like that. Hold on.”
Just then I heard the sound of Rafuemon about to pull some gadget out. Oh, and I’ve just become able to use Chaos Stab and Second Javelin.
“Why do you even own such a useless gadget! Itsuki! Stop Rafuemon!”
“Mysterious magic tools from the future—there’s something dreamy about that, isn’t there.”
“I wonder what it says about Rafuemon-san that he pulls stuff out the moment someone says ‘I want to cosplay.’”
“Well, the sky’s free to fly through, after all.”
“Don’t bring that one out, please. Rafuemon-san, that one’s a hassle too, so no need to bring it out.”
“Is that so?”
I pressed steadily onward, listening to Father and the others’ idle chatter. Partway through… I heard a sizzling sound, the sound of Father cooking.
“That’s the sound of Father cooking, I say!”
“Ah, yeah. Figured everyone would be getting hungry soon, so I’m cooking with Ren and Gaelion-chan.”
“Rival, you mean?”
“Having her breathe out a low flame from underneath the frying pan.”
“Nano—”
I heard the dull whoosh of Rival breathing fire.
“Might as well go back to the castle for this one, honestly. Watching food arrive while I watch someone else’s playthrough footage isn’t bad either.”
“Itsuki! I demand a change!”
“No, no, Motoyasu-san, please press onward.”

Argh! That Itsuki—is he out of range or something, that he can’t switch with me! For that matter, Ren can’t switch either! It’s Father’s cooking time, I say! Not being able to smell that fragrant aroma, only hear it through my ears—that’s quite the hardship, I say!
“Once it’s done, I’ll switch you out with Motoyasu-kun, so don’t worry.”
I got to hear Father’s kind words. And so, as I pressed on defeating monsters…
“Ah… a rare drop, huh.”
Ren muttered this after defeating an illusion of some low-tier monster called a Wipughost, a weak enemy that looked like a ghost wearing a cloth over its head.
“What? Did something drop? Sounds like only Ren reacted to it.”
“It’s a sword called Vacuugast. Seems it fell under the sword category, so it reacted to me.”
“Bad ring to the name. What kind of sword is it?”
“The base attack is decent enough, but… nothing especially impressive. The release effect boosts speed too, but it’s nothing dramatic. It just has one unique effect—Four Consecutive Slashes.”
“Huh, try it out for a sec.”
“Sure.”
With that, I heard what sounded like Ren doing a practice swing. Shu-shu-shun! went the sound.
“Sounds like a single swing sends out three wind blades chasing the target.”
Being out on the front lines, it was a shame I couldn’t see it myself.
“…Ren, isn’t that a seriously broken weapon?”
“Huh? This, broken?”

“I mean, a single swing chains three attacks in a row, right? Just casually swinging it keeps racking up hit count—if you base a weapon on that, or transplant that unique effect through synthesis, you’d get four attacks per swing all the time. Whether it even applies to skills is something we’d need to test.”
“W-Wait, Air Strike Bash!”
“Even so, I doubt a skill would fire four times.”
“Right? So this can’t possibly be a broken weapon.”

“No, no, even during a skill’s cooldown, the normal attacks alone would keep enemies from closing in—that’s strong. I mean, even if Itsuki fires an arrow or a bullet, this thing could probably intercept it with high odds.”
“Eh? Eh? Eh?”
Ren seemed to be swinging his sword wildly at random, because the whooshing sound just kept going and going.
